Ascites:-\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003EPeritoneovenous shunt \u003C\/b\u003Eplacement is performed as a long- term treatment for chronic refractory ascites. The shunt used most commonly is the Denver shunt, comprised of two silastic tubes connected by a compressible pump.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv class=\"separator\" style=\"clear: both; text-align: center;\"\u003E\n \u003Ca href=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgQ2HQnSllPP_l9GMKjLbXqEyyb8u1jWdgth9PtbEBHI-3zvMJw0DGu-mEJaNMXl-wm3jiItmWSiCFe9cJTlF4x2gzq2YVqdwQeHANiiViQPP22BhmLglcqCY8xUNIDIp487hvcABUM7SxJiVyZi6H-qcxt01i0puAYHLFwHbPC_pj33nO7kjwmWm2UZWo\" imageanchor=\"1\" style=\"margin-left: 1em; margin-right: 1em;\"\u003E\n \u003Cimg border=\"0\" src=\"https:\/\/blogger.googleusercontent.com\/img\/a\/AVvXsEgQ2HQnSllPP_l9GMKjLbXqEyyb8u1jWdgth9PtbEBHI-3zvMJw0DGu-mEJaNMXl-wm3jiItmWSiCFe9cJTlF4x2gzq2YVqdwQeHANiiViQPP22BhmLglcqCY8xUNIDIp487hvcABUM7SxJiVyZi6H-qcxt01i0puAYHLFwHbPC_pj33nO7kjwmWm2UZWo\" width=\"400\"\u003E\n \u003C\/a\u003E\n\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E**Indications\u003C\/b\u003E\u003Cb\u003E:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPVS is effective in the drainage of the peritoneal fluid in patients with chronic refractory ascites. The most common indication for insertion of PVS is medically intractable ascites secondary to chronic liver diseases. Conditions that result in chronic ascites that is unresponsive to medical therapy are best treated with PVS. These include acute and chronic liver diseases like cirrhosis, malignant ascites due to malignant tumors of the breast, ovary, or colon, chylous ascites, congestive heart failure, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and portal vein thrombosis.PVS is indicated under the following conditions:\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;Malignant or cirrhotic ascites unresponsive to medical treatment and large volume paracentesis\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;Chylous ascites\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;The patient is unresponsive to diuretics.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;The patient is not a candidate for liver transplantation.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;The patient is not a candidate for serial therapeutic paracentesis due to extensive abdominal surgical scars.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;The patient has a life expectancy of more than three months.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;The patient has no contraindication to PVS.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E-\u0026gt;Non-availability of physicians to perform serial therapeutic paracentesis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003ETechnique:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe most commonly used PVS is the Denver shunt, which a modified version of the original design. After the patient is prepped and draped, an all-purpose drainage (APD) catheter is inserted at the upper abdominal region to drain the ascitic fluid. It is then replaced with the peritoneal end of the shunt after priming it with warmed saline. It is inserted between the right hepatic lobe and the ribs. The second incision is made on the lower rib cage for the placement of the compressible pump. It must be placed against a firm, stable rib for effective compression. The third incision is made at the venous access site. Using a long metallic tunneler, the shunt is traversed towards the neck, ideally subcutaneously; however, it can also be placed percutaneously.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe venous end of the shunt is inserted into the superior vena cava via the internal jugular veins or the subclavian veins under fluoroscopic guidance until the catheter tip ends in the proximal right atrium. A one-way pressure-sensitive valve is attached to prevent the backflow of blood from the venous end of the shunt.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cu\u003E4.\u003Cb\u003EComplications from PVS:-\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;Common and include:-\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPeritoneal Infection,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EVariceal Bleeding,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ESuperior Vena Cava Thrombosis,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPulmonary Edema,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDisseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC), Scar Tissue Formation,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EShunt fracture,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EOcclusion,\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EDisplacement or Leakage,\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EPneumothorax, and Pneumoperitoneum.\u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EThe \u003Cb\u003Emost common\u003C\/b\u003E complication of PVS is \u003Cb\u003EShunt Occlusion\u003C\/b\u003E, with only 18.6% of shunts remaining patent at two years, according to a study.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EAbout 9% of the patients report with disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) after shunt insertion.This condition may be due to the presence of activating factors like tissue factor (TF) that initiate thrombogenesis. Thrombosis of the shunt is a rare occurrence and mainly involves the tip of the venous end of the shunt.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EStaphylococcal and gram-negative organisms can result in perioperative infections, which may progress to bacterial peritonitis or sepsis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EB)Learning Points in Long Case:-\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E1. Here we discuss our individual patient problem through series of inputs from available global online community of experts with an aim to solve those patients clinical problem with collective current best evidence input.\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;This E blog also reflect my patient centered online learning portfolia and your valuable inputs on the comment box is welcome.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;I have been given this case to solve in an attempts to understand the topic of patient clinical data analysis to develop my compentency in reading and comphrending clinical data including history , clinical finding , investigation and come up with diagnosis and treatment plan....\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EA 29 year old male from Miryalaguda ,a agricultural woker by occupation came to opd with complaints of \u003Ci\u003EBilateral pain in lower limbs upto knee since 22 days\u003C\/i\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EHistory of Presenting Illness:-\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp; \u0026nbsp;Patient was apparently asymptomatic 3 years ago then he developed severe sudden pain in right lower abdomen which is insidious in onset and gradually progressive for that he went to local hospital and was diagnosed to\u0026nbsp; have renal calculus of 4 - 6 mm and relived on Medications. Then \u003Ci\u003Eafter 6 months\u003C\/i\u003E he developed \u003Ci\u003Epain in lower limbs bilaterally\u003C\/i\u003E\u0026nbsp;which is stabbing type and aggrevated by heavy work\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E(Like lifting heavy weights) for which he visited a local doctor and was tested the results shows high uric acid levels for which he used medications and relieved. Then he also had history of lower limb pain which is intermittent\u0026nbsp; for which he used Tab.Acyclophenac whenever he was having episodes of pain. Since 22 days pain is not\u0026nbsp; reliving on medication and he got admitted to a local hospital his creatinine levels were 8.2 and then he referred to our hospital for Dialysis.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPast history:-\u003C\/u\u003E\u003C\/b\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u0026nbsp;3 years ago he had lower abdomen pain and he diagnosed fir having renal stones of 4 mm size and relieved on medication.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003EHistory of Rat poisoning 5 years ago.\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003ENot a known case of Diabetes,hypertension,Asthma,TB,CVD, Epilepsy and CVA.\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cbr\u003E\u003C\/div\u003E\u003Cdiv\u003E\u003Cb\u003E\u003Cu\u003EPersonal
